issue.title: Content-Type header must be allowed explicitly, docs say otherwise

issue.body:
According to [1], "The Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Language and Content-Type headers are always allowed for CORS requests."

This is not the currently implemented behavior according to the test below.

```python
def test_cors_always_allow_content_type():
    app = Starlette()

    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=["https://example.org"],
        allow_headers=[],
    )

    @app.route("/")
    def homepage(request):
        return PlainTextResponse("Homepage", status_code=200)

    client = TestClient(app)

    # Test pre-flight response
    headers = {
        "Origin": "https://example.org",
        "Access-Control-Request-Method": "GET",
        "Access-Control-Request-Headers": "Content-Type",
    }
    response = client.options("/", headers=headers)
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.text == "OK"
    assert response.headers["access-control-allow-origin"] == "https://example.org"
    assert response.headers["access-control-allow-headers"] == "Content-Type"
```

The test fails with

```
        }
        response = client.options("/", headers=headers)
>       assert response.status_code == 200
E       assert 400 == 200
E        +  where 400 = <Response [400]>.status_code

tests/middleware/test_cors.py:115: AssertionError
```

[1] https://www.starlette.io/middleware/#corsmiddleware
